title: CDL driver qualifications practice questions
description: Free CDL driver qualifications practice questions on 49 CFR Part 391. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Except as provided in subpart G, what minimum age does 391.11(b)(1) set for a person to be qualified to drive a commercial motor vehicle?

options.B: 16 years old
options.C: 17 years old
options.D: There is no minimum age in Part 391

questions.explanation: Except as provided in subpart G, a person is qualified only if he or she "Is at least 21 years old".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.11, General qualifications of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except as provided in subpart G of this part, a person is qualified to drive a motor vehicle if he/she— (1) Is at least 21 years old;

questions.question: What does 391.11(b)(2) require of a driver regarding the English language?

options.A: Being able to speak English; reading it is not required
options.B: Being able to read English traffic signs; speaking it is not required
options.C: Being able to read and speak it sufficiently to converse with the general public, understand highway traffic signs and signals, respond to official inquiries, and make entries on reports and records
options.D: Nothing; a driver may rely on an interpreter for all official inquiries

questions.explanation: The driver must be able to "read and speak the English language sufficiently to converse with the general public, to understand highway traffic signs and signals in the English language, to respond to official inquiries, and to make entries on reports and records".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.11, General qualifications of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Can read and speak the English language sufficiently to converse with the general public, to understand highway traffic signs and signals in the English language, to respond to official inquiries, and to make entries on reports and records;

questions.question: A driver receives a notice that his CMV license has been suspended. What deadline does 391.15(b)(2) set for telling the motor carrier that employs him about the notice?

options.B: Before the end of the business day following the day he received it
options.C: At the motor carrier's next annual review of his driving record
options.D: Only if the suspension lasts longer than 90 days

questions.explanation: The driver must notify the motor carrier that employs him or her "of the contents of the notice before the end of the business day following the day the driver received it."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.15, Disqualification of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A driver who receives a notice that his/her license, permit, or privilege to operate a commercial motor vehicle has been revoked, suspended, or withdrawn shall notify the motor carrier that employs him/ her of the contents of the notice before the end of the business day following the day the driver received it.

questions.question: What alcohol concentration threshold does 391.15(c)(2)(i)(A) set for driving a CMV while under the influence of alcohol?

options.B: 0.15 percent or more
options.C: 0.20 percent or more
options.D: 0.04 percent or more

questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol includes "Driving a commercial motor vehicle while the person's alcohol concentration is 0.04 percent or more".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.15, Disqualification of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Driving a commercial motor vehicle while the person's alcohol concentration is 0.04 percent or more;

questions.question: Under 391.15(c)(3)(i), what disqualification period applies to a first offender, when the conviction did not solely concern transportation or possession of the substances in (c)(2)(iii)?

options.B: 1 year after the date of conviction or forfeiture
options.C: 10 years
options.D: Lifetime, with no reinstatement

questions.explanation: "A driver is disqualified for 1 year after the date of conviction or forfeiture of bond or collateral" if there was no disqualifying conviction or forfeiture in the 3 years before; the period is 6 months only when the case "soley concerned the transportation or possession" of the listed substances.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.15, Disqualification of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: First offenders. A driver is disqualified for 1 year after the date of conviction or forfeiture of bond or collateral if, during the 3 years preceding that date, the driver was not convicted of, or did not forfeit bond or collateral upon a charge of an offense that would disqualify the driver under the rules of this section. Exemption. The period of disqualification is 6 months if the conviction or forfeiture of bond or collateral soley concerned the transportation or possession of substances named in paragraph (c)(2)(iii) of this section.

questions.question: A driver who was not transporting placarded hazardous materials or operating a vehicle designed to transport more than 15 passengers is convicted of a first violation of an out-of-service order. What disqualification range does 391.15(d)(2)(i) set?

options.A: Not less than 90 days nor more than one year
options.B: Not less than 1 day nor more than 10 days
options.C: Not less than 10 years nor more than 20 years
options.D: A warning only, with no disqualification

questions.explanation: "A driver is disqualified for not less than 90 days nor more than one year if the driver is convicted of a first violation of an out-of-service order."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.15, Disqualification of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: First violation. A driver is disqualified for not less than 90 days nor more than one year if the driver is convicted of a first violation of an out-of-service order.

questions.question: What disqualification does 391.15(e)(2)(i) set for a driver convicted of two violations of the texting prohibition in 392.80(a) in separate incidents during any 3-year period?

options.B: 14 days
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 60 days

questions.explanation: "A driver is disqualified for 60 days if the driver is convicted of two violations of § 392.80(a) of this chapter in separate incidents during any 3-year period."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.15, Disqualification of drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Second violation. A driver is disqualified for 60 days if the driver is convicted of two violations of § 392.80(a) of this chapter in separate incidents during any 3-year period.

questions.question: Under 391.21(b), on what form must the driver's application for employment be made, and who must complete and sign it?

options.A: A form furnished by FMCSA, completed and signed by the motor carrier
options.B: A form furnished by the State licensing agency, signed by a medical examiner
options.C: A form furnished by the motor carrier, completed and signed by the applicant
options.D: Any form, completed by the motor carrier and signed by the previous employer

questions.explanation: "The application for employment shall be made on a form furnished by the motor carrier. Each application form must be completed by the applicant, must be signed by him/her".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.21, Application for employment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The application for employment shall be made on a form furnished by the motor carrier. Each application form must be completed by the applicant, must be signed by him/her, and must contain the following information:

questions.question: Except as provided in subpart G, what time limit does 391.23(a)(1) set for the motor carrier's inquiry to licensing authorities for a newly employed driver's motor vehicle record?

options.A: Within 30 days of the date the driver's employment begins
options.B: Within 6 months of the date the driver's employment begins
options.C: Within 1 year of the date the driver's employment begins
options.D: At the end of the driver's first 2 years of employment

questions.explanation: The carrier makes "An inquiry, within 30 days of the date the driver's employment begins, to each driver's licensing authority where the driver held or holds a motor vehicle operator's license or permit during the preceding 3 years".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.23, Investigation and inquiries (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An inquiry, within 30 days of the date the driver's employment begins, to each driver's licensing authority where the driver held or holds a motor vehicle operator's license or permit during the preceding 3 years, to obtain that driver's motor vehicle record covering that driver's prior 3-year driving history.

questions.question: Under 391.23(f)(1), what must a prospective motor carrier employer do if a driver refuses to provide consent for release of the alcohol and controlled substances information from previous employers?

options.A: Let the driver operate a CMV for up to 30 days while it asks again
options.B: Not permit the driver to operate a commercial motor vehicle for that motor carrier
options.C: Let the driver operate a CMV if the driver passes a road test
options.D: Ask the State licensing agency to give consent on the driver's behalf

questions.explanation: "If the driver refuses to provide this consent, the prospective motor carrier employer must not permit the driver to operate a commercial motor vehicle for that motor carrier."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.23, Investigation and inquiries (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the driver refuses to provide this consent, the prospective motor carrier employer must not permit the driver to operate a commercial motor vehicle for that motor carrier.

questions.question: Except as provided in subpart G, what does 391.25(a) require for the motor carrier's periodic inquiry for each driver's motor vehicle record?

options.A: An inquiry once every 3 years, covering the preceding 3 years
options.B: An inquiry once every 5 years, covering the preceding 5 years
options.C: An inquiry only when the driver changes license States
options.D: An inquiry at least once every 12 months, covering at least the preceding 12 months

questions.explanation: Each motor carrier "shall, at least once every 12 months, make an inquiry to obtain the motor vehicle record of each driver it employs, covering at least the preceding 12 months".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.25, Annual inquiry and review of driving record (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: each motor carrier shall, at least once every 12 months, make an inquiry to obtain the motor vehicle record of each driver it employs, covering at least the preceding 12 months, to each driver's licensing authority where the driver held a commercial motor vehicle operator's license or permit during the time period.

questions.question: In the annual review of a driver's record, to which violations does 391.25(b)(2) say the motor carrier must give great weight?

options.B: Violations committed in a personal vehicle more than 10 years ago only
options.C: Violations, such as speeding, reckless driving, and operating while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, that indicate a disregard for the safety of the public
options.D: Equipment violations found at roadside inspections only

questions.explanation: The carrier "must give great weight to violations, such as speeding, reckless driving, and operating while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, that indicate that the driver has exhibited a disregard for the safety of the public."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.25, Annual inquiry and review of driving record (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: must give great weight to violations, such as speeding, reckless driving, and operating while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, that indicate that the driver has exhibited a disregard for the safety of the public.

questions.question: Under 391.31(b), who must give the road test to a driver who is also a motor carrier?

options.A: The driver himself or herself, as long as the road test form is signed
options.B: Nobody; a driver who is a motor carrier is exempt from the road test
options.C: Any passenger, whether or not competent to evaluate the driver
options.D: A person other than himself or herself

questions.explanation: "However, a driver who is a motor carrier must be given the test by a person other than himself/herself." The tester must also be "competent to evaluate and determine" the driver's ability.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.31, Road test (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: However, a driver who is a motor carrier must be given the test by a person other than himself/herself. The test shall be given by a person who is competent to evaluate and determine whether the person who takes the test has demonstrated that he/she is capable of operating the commercial motor vehicle, and associated equipment, that the motor carrier intends to assign him/her.

questions.question: Under 391.33(a)(2), a motor carrier may accept as equivalent to the road test a copy of a valid certificate of driver's road test issued under 391.31. What issue period does the rule set for that certificate?

options.B: The preceding 5 years
options.C: The preceding 10 years
options.D: Any time, with no limit

questions.explanation: The carrier may accept "A copy of a valid certificate of driver's road test issued to him/her pursuant to § 391.31 within the preceding 3 years."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.33, Equivalent of road test (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A copy of a valid certificate of driver's road test issued to him/her pursuant to § 391.31 within the preceding 3 years.

questions.question: Under the vision standard in 391.41(b)(10)(i), what distant visual acuity is required in each eye, without corrective lenses or separately corrected with them?

options.B: At least 20/40 (Snellen)
options.C: At least 20/80 (Snellen)
options.D: At least 20/200 (Snellen)

questions.explanation: The standard is "distant visual acuity of at least 20/40 (Snellen) in each eye without corrective lenses or visual acuity separately corrected to 20/40 (Snellen) or better with corrective lenses". A person who, with the worse eye, does not satisfy the acuity standard with corrective lenses or the field of vision standard may instead meet 391.44.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.41, Physical qualifications for drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Has distant visual acuity of at least 20/40 (Snellen) in each eye without corrective lenses or visual acuity separately corrected to 20/40 (Snellen) or better with corrective lenses

questions.question: For the forced whispered voice test in 391.41(b)(11), what distance does the rule set for first perceiving the voice in the better ear?

options.B: Not less than 2 feet
options.C: Not less than 5 feet
options.D: Not less than 3 feet

questions.explanation: The driver "First perceives a forced whispered voice in the better ear at not less than 5 feet with or without the use of a hearing aid" (an audiometric test is the other option).

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.41, Physical qualifications for drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: First perceives a forced whispered voice in the better ear at not less than 5 feet with or without the use of a hearing aid

questions.question: How does 391.41(b)(6) state the physical qualification standard for high blood pressure?

options.A: Any blood pressure reading above 120/80 disqualifies the driver
options.B: The person has no current clinical diagnosis of high blood pressure likely to interfere with his/her ability to operate a CMV safely
options.C: High blood pressure is not mentioned in the physical qualification standards
options.D: The driver must take blood pressure medication before every trip

questions.explanation: A person is physically qualified if he or she "Has no current clinical diagnosis of high blood pressure likely to interfere with his/her ability to operate a commercial motor vehicle safely".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.41, Physical qualifications for drivers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Has no current clinical diagnosis of high blood pressure likely to interfere with his/her ability to operate a commercial motor vehicle safely;

questions.question: Except as provided in 391.43(b), who must perform the medical examination of a CMV driver?

options.B: A State driver licensing clerk
options.C: An FMCSA safety investigator
options.D: A medical examiner listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners

questions.explanation: "Except as provided by paragraph (b) of this section, the medical examination must be performed by a medical examiner listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.43, Medical examination; certificate of physical examination (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except as provided by paragraph (b) of this section, the medical examination must be performed by a medical examiner listed on the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners under subpart D of part 390 of this chapter.

questions.question: Under 391.45(b), unless a paragraph with a different schedule applies, a driver must be medically examined and certified if he or she has not been examined and certified during what preceding period?

options.B: 36 months
options.C: 48 months
options.D: 60 months

questions.explanation: Examination is required for "Any driver who has not been medically examined and certified as qualified to operate a commercial motor vehicle during the preceding 24 months", unless paragraph (c), (e), (f), (g), or (h) applies.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.45, Persons who must be medically examined and certified (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any driver who has not been medically examined and certified as qualified to operate a commercial motor vehicle during the preceding 24 months, unless the driver is required to be examined and certified in accordance with paragraph (c), (e), (f), (g), or (h) of this section;

questions.question: Except as provided in 391.51(d), how long does 391.51(c) say a driver's qualification file must be retained?

options.A: Only while the driver is employed by that motor carrier
options.B: For 1 year after the driver's employment ends
options.C: For as long as the driver is employed by that motor carrier and for three years thereafter
options.D: Until the driver's license next expires

questions.explanation: "Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, each driver's qualification file shall be retained for as long as a driver is employed by that motor carrier and for three years thereafter."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 391.51, General requirements for driver qualification files (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except as provided in paragraph (d) of this section, each driver's qualification file shall be retained for as long as a driver is employed by that motor carrier and for three years thereafter.
